note: Only after a preposition: para ti, de ti. With con it becomes contigo.

sent.en: This is for you.

note: con and mí fuse into one word. Never con mí.

sent.en: Do you want to come with me?

note: The informal one. With usted it stays con usted.

sent.en: I want to talk to you.

note: The indirect object for more than one person, ustedes included. Before lo or la it turns into se.

sent.en: I sent them all a message.

note: Only when the whole group is female. One man in the group and it is ellos.

sent.en: They live in Medellín.

note: Only when everyone in the group is female.

sent.en: We arrived first.

note: Agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: mío, mía, míos, mías.

sent.en: That book is mine.

note: Informal yours. Agrees with the thing owned: tuyo, tuya.

sent.en: Is this phone yours?

note: Also the polite yours, for usted. Agrees with the thing owned: suyo, suya.

sent.en: It is not her fault.

note: Before an adjective or adverb: tan bonito. tan ... como is as ... as.

sent.en: The food is so good.

note: ni ... ni is neither ... nor. ni siquiera is not even.

sent.en: I have neither the time nor the money.

note: A filler Colombians use constantly, often at the end of a sentence: sí, pues.

sent.en: Well, I do not know what to say.

note: Only after a negative, to correct it: no es rojo sino azul.

sent.es: No es mi hermano {sino} mi primo.
sent.en: He is not my brother but my cousin.

note: Direction rather than destination: a gets you there, hacia only points.

sent.en: We walked towards the park.

sent.es: Mañana jugamos {contra} un equipo de Cali.
sent.en: Tomorrow we play against a team from Cali.

note: On its own it also means it depends: ¿vas a ir? Según.

sent.en: According to the map, it is close.

note: Usually at the start of the sentence, with a comma after it.

sent.es: Es caro. {Sin embargo}, vale la pena.
sent.en: It is expensive. However, it is worth it.

note: Adds a further point, often at the start: además, es barato.

sent.en: Besides, the hotel is very cheap.

note: Before the surprising part: incluso los niños.

sent.en: Even the children know it.

note: hasta pronto is see you soon.

sent.en: See you soon.

note: The next step in a sequence: primero esto, luego aquello.

sent.en: First we eat and then we go out.

note: Agrees like an adjective: juntos, juntas.

sent.en: We are going to have dinner together tonight.

note: In Colombia also anyway: igual voy, I am going anyway. me da igual is I do not mind.

sent.es: Tu camisa es {igual} a la mía.
sent.en: Your shirt is the same as mine.

note: Same meaning as todavía. Without the accent, aun means even.

sent.en: The bus has not arrived yet.

note: Same as tal vez. Often takes the subjunctive: quizás llueva.

sent.en: Perhaps it will rain tomorrow.

note: Literally at times.

sent.en: Sometimes I work from home.

note: Literally another time. de nuevo means the same.

sent.en: Tell me again, please.

note: Colombians often say seguido instead.

sent.en: I often go to the gym.

note: In Colombia it can also mean maybe: de repente llueve.

sent.en: Suddenly it started to rain.

note: al menos means the same.

sent.en: Wait at least ten minutes.

note: Before an adjective it is too: demasiado caro. Before a noun it agrees: demasiada gente.

sent.en: This hotel is too expensive.

note: Before a noun. On its own, or after one, it is cualquiera.

sent.en: You can call me at any time.

note: Shortens to ningún before a masculine noun: ningún problema. Needs no before the verb.

sent.en: I do not have any problem.

note: Agrees: ambos, ambas.

sent.en: They both speak English.

note: Agrees: varios días, varias veces.

sent.en: I have several friends in Bogotá.

note: For something far from both of you. Agrees: aquel, aquella, aquellos.

sent.en: Can you see that building over there?

note: Use it rather than qué before ser: ¿cuál es tu número?

sent.en: Which one is your car?

note: Genuinely, in fact. For really? as a reaction, say ¿en serio?

sent.en: I really do not mind.
I will probably be late.

note: On its own as a reply, exacto is more natural.

sent.en: That is exactly what I want.

note: por fin is the more everyday at last.

sent.en: I finally found the keys.
I simply do not have time.

note: On the subject of. sobre does the same job and is commoner.

sent.en: We talked about the film.

note: alrededor de before a noun.

sent.en: There are shops around the square.

note: detrás de before a noun.

sent.es: El baño está {detrás} de la cocina.
sent.en: The bathroom is behind the kitchen.

note: delante de before a noun. enfrente is facing you, often across a street.

sent.es: Hay un carro {delante} de la casa.
sent.en: There is a car in front of the house.

note: encima de before a noun.

sent.es: Las llaves están {encima} de la mesa.
sent.en: The keys are on top of the table.

note: debajo de before a noun.

sent.es: El gato está {debajo} de la cama.
sent.en: The cat is under the bed.

note: mi hermano mayor is my older brother. el mayor is the oldest.

sent.en: My older brother lives in London.

note: la menor is the youngest.

sent.es: Ella es la {menor} de la familia.
sent.en: She is the youngest in the family.

note: Both the ordinal and the unit of time: un segundo.

sent.en: I live on the second floor.

note: Shortens to tercer before a masculine noun: el tercer día.

sent.en: It is the third time I have called.

note: m. un par de días is a couple of days.

sent.es: Me quedo un {par} de días más.
sent.en: I am staying a couple more days.

note: m. The remainder. To rest is descansar.

sent.en: I will tell you the rest tomorrow.

note: f. The noun. As an adjective, half is medio: media hora.

sent.en: I have already read half the book.
